title: Psychiatrist visit
what: A doctor who helps with problems of mood, anxiety, sleep, thinking, and behavior. They can prescribe treatment and medicines.
why: For long-lasting low mood, severe anxiety, panic attacks, insomnia, obsessive thoughts, or sudden changes in behavior.
tell_doctor: What bothers you, and for how long
What medicines and substances you take, including alcohol
Past visits to a psychiatrist or psychologist

prepare.title: Write it down
prepare.text: What bothers you, how it affects your life, and what questions you want to ask.

prepare.title: Confidentiality
prepare.text: What happens at the visit is confidential. Ask the clinic how the visit is recorded.

bring: Past test results, discharge papers, and reports
A list of your medicines, or the packs themselves
steps: The doctor calmly asks about your concerns and your life
You are asked about mood, sleep, and thoughts
Sometimes you fill in a questionnaire
The doctor explains what is going on and what help is available
If needed, treatment is prescribed and the next visit set
feel: It is a conversation, with no procedures
Talking about personal things can be hard. You can take pauses
after: Take medicines as prescribed. Do not stop them on your own. Ask the doctor
Treatment usually takes time to work
red_flags: Thoughts of harming yourself or someone else: do not wait for the visit. Call emergency services

faq.q: Will I be put on a psychiatric register?
faq.a: A consultation usually does not mean that. Ask the clinic directly how it works.

faq.q: How is a psychiatrist different from a psychologist?
faq.a: A psychiatrist is a doctor who can diagnose and prescribe medicines. A psychologist helps through talking and does not prescribe.

reminders.text: Psychiatrist visit tomorrow. Write down what bothers you, and bring your medicine list.
